body:
Frame duration is a critical property for making FMV games to keep gameplay and playback in sync and process user input events to the frame data so I think this should be in some way exposed.

Related to that note that this was not part of PR (salvage) https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114515 that exposed nearly all playback api for script control because we have no general API defined for some important video properties.

If we do add this here it makes sense to add at the base stream/playback class level as it is a generic property that every single new and old VideoStream class (e.g. theora, webm) should have.

If we place this only on theora no video player or gameplay like FMV can reliably work with this function as they all need to check what stream type it is and if they have that function.

(Note for upvote bean counter reviewers rafael coded this on stream hence the reactions on this PR are inflated in count due to streamer audience)

> (Note for upvote bean counter reviewers rafael coded this on stream hence the reactions on this PR are inflated in count due to streamer audience)

I disagree with this, people have been waiting for this in Godot for a long time, video support in Godot is quite crude, and any investment in this area is welcomed by the people.

> Frame duration is a critical property for making FMV games to keep gameplay and playback in sync and process user input events to the frame data so I think this should be in some way exposed.

Cool! That's our motivation.

> Related to that note that this was not part of PR (salvage) #114515 that exposed nearly all playback api for script control because we have no general API defined for some important video properties.
> 
> If we do add this here it makes sense to add at the base stream/playback class level as it is a generic property that every single new and old VideoStream class (e.g. theora, webm) should have.
> 
> If we place this only on theora no video player or gameplay like FMV can reliably work with this function as they all need to check what stream type it is and if they have that function.

At this moment, there's only one codec available on the engine and it's Theora. But, as you can see on the PR files, we also modified the "VideoStream" and "VideoStreamPlayback" to make this PR upstream. If anybody is adapting or creating a codec for Godot, they should implement a way to expose the frame_duration value. I think that this small change is easy to apply and it benefits many people.

I'm developing an addon to add WebM support (with alpha channel)... so I will implement it use it on the addon. 

> (Note for upvote bean counter reviewers rafael coded this on stream hence the reactions on this PR are inflated in count due to streamer audience)

I have a Godot community, and I'm followed by Godot creators interested in this. Some of them upload their creations here on GitHub, so they voted. But people outside my stream/community have also voted.

FMV is one of my recurring themes; so much so that we've revived an FMV arcade game from the '90s (with a modern adaptation using Godot), and I'm currently developing a FMV Engine with a Visual Editor... all of this live on Twitch.

I decided to submit a Pull Request thinking that, by following the rules, there wouldn't be any major problems, and after verifying that there are no performance or security issues, I believe it should be considered for approval.

> I'm developing an addon to add WebM support (with alpha channel)... so I will implement it use it on the addon.

WebM support was removed in Godot 4 not because it was not wanted but because the used third party was complete outdated, the implementation had a lot of bugs that even crashed user projects and zero maintainer available to fix any of that. The user complains stacked up so at some point it was decided to remove it instead of keeping its broken state. If someone would show up to create a lean and working WebM module I am sure there are real chances it can be added back in.

> I'm developing an addon to add WebM support (with alpha channel)... so I will implement it use it on the addon.
@rafalagoon

This isn't about the original PR (sorry) but you may want to take a look at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119299, which is a PR attempting to add back WebM support in the core engine.
If you are experienced with working on video processing, help on the PR would be very useful. Otherwise, you might find the PR helpful in creating your addon.
